title: Real minimizer conjecture for nearest Hurwitz-stable matrices
statement:
Let $S_{\Omega_H,n,\mathbb{C}}$ denote the set of complex $n\times n$ Hurwitz-stable matrices, and let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$. Consider the Frobenius-norm minimization problem

$$
B=\arg\min_{X\in S_{\Omega_H,n,\mathbb{C}}}\lVert X-A\rVert_F^2.
$$

**Real minimizer conjecture.** The problem has a real solution $B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$.
The conjecture concerns whether minimizing over all complex matrices can always be achieved by a real matrix when the target matrix is real. The authors report that this occurred in all of their limited numerical experiments, but note that the nonconvexity of the Hurwitz-stable set makes a proof non-obvious; the supplied text gives no resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.07052

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).
source_name: Vanni Noferini and Federico Poloni, “Nearest Ω-stable matrix via Riemannian optimization”, arXiv:2002.07052 (2021).
